Amitagati
Jain. Dig. pupil of Mādhavasena of the Māthura Saṅgha; wrote his Subhāṣitaratnasandoha (see last verse) in 993 A. D. when king Muñja was ruling; wrote his Dharmaparīkṣā in 1013 A. D. (see MD. 5381) an. his Pañcasaṅgraha in 1017 A. D. [Page344-a.
--Upāsakācāra or Śrāvakācāra. Delhi III. 52. Hombucca 40 (a.. Moodbidri II. 31. 157. 257. 299 (a..
Pt.. in Anantakīrti Granthamālā 2, Bombay, 1922.
--Dvātriṁśatikā or Dvātriṁśībhāvanā or Bhāvanādvātriṁśatikā. CPB. 7725. 7726. Peters. V. p. 308 (no. 925 (2)).
Ed.. Mānik. Dig. Jain. Granth. 13, p.. 132 ff.
--Dharmaparīkṣā. AK. 1091. CPB. 7423-29. Moodbidri II. 192 (a.. MT. 5381. Peters. III. p. 402 (no. 513). Extr. p.. 294-7. Śravanabelgola 300. Weber 2019.
For a study see N. Miranov, Strassburg, 1903.
--Pañcasaṅgraha.
Ed.. Mānik. Dig. Jain Granth. 25, 1927.
--Paramātmasvarūpa. Moodbidri I. 243.
--Bhagavatyārādhanā, a Skt. version of a Pkt. work of that name of Śivakoṭyācārya. Pannalal Bombay II. p. 46.
Pt.. a. Sholapur.
--Yogasāra (Bṛhat). Jhalrapatan p. 9.
Ed.. Sanātana Jaina Granthamālā 16, 1918.
--Sāmayikapāṭha. Pt.. in Mānik. Dig. Jain Granth. 21, 1922.
The real name of the work seems to have been Tattvabhāvanā an. it seems from its own col. to have formed part of a bigger work. The Dvātriṁśatikābhāvanā is oftentimes called also by the name Sāmayikapāṭha from which one may suppose that the two formed part of the bigger work.
--Subhāṣitaratnasandoha. [Page344-b]
Edn.. (1) K. M. 82. (2) Leipzig, 1908. See also ZDMG. 1905 an. 1907.
On Amitagati an. his works, see Jaina Sid. Bhās. VII. i. p.. 29-36, an. Intro. p. 71. fn. 3, edn. of Paramārthaprakāśa, Rāyacandra Jaina Śāstramālā, 10, where it is suggested that Sāmayikapāṭha an. Yogasāra may be works of Amitagati I, who was grandpreceptor of this a., Amitagati II.
